explanation: Hosted lowering escapes a stored string into the arena; native strings are tiered immutable shares. String escapes are not copies under the copy policy in either compiler.
Both compilers copy on this row; they name the boundary, the kind (a tag cell against the record it holds) or the reason differently.
Hosted unions keep payloads inline with per-union family slots, so widening or storing a union value retags it by copying. Native cells hold one handle under program-wide tags and share it.
site: ^(converted to a union|stored in a union)$

explanation: A policy-exempt note for a record or tag cell that adopts owned handles (a move with a new root). One compiler records it as a copy note, the other moves without one or shares.
reason: adopts|promotes storage before the owner dies|bounded scalar cell

explanation: Native reads a field through a temporary or a selected union field that needs its own storage; hosted reads the field in place.
reason: temporary that holds it|selected field needs independent storage|result must own its payload

explanation: A `get` result owns its payload. Native shares a headed block and copies the rest; hosted copies record payloads.
Each compiler proves some last-use moves the other does not (place loans, union payloads, flow results). Each difference is a proof precision gap tracked under row C2/C3.
reason: used again|not a local|still live or cannot transfer

explanation: One compiler proves a read-only view of a container's element or field where the other copies. A borrow proof precision gap.
One compiler borrows an argument the other copies: callee summaries (writes, keeps, unresolved callee) differ in precision.
reason: not borrowed here|the body (writes|keeps|needs)|another argument of the same call

explanation: A value read from storage that belongs to something else (a global, a parameter's field) is copied by one compiler and borrowed by the other.

An explicit `.copy` authorizes a copy; it does not require one. Native code elides an explicit copy whose source is already independent (a popped entry, a node read from its arena) or whose result is only read; hosted lowering performs it. A cost difference, not a semantic one.
